doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: NASA celebration and accepting that life is a struggle
summary: Jones describes an upcoming NASA event with the astronauts, says you cannot start or stop what happens, and quotes M. Scott Peck and Basie on hills and valleys.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: a celebration with Neil Armstrong, John Glenn – who I run crazy, because I ask him so many questions, because nobody else has seen what he’s seen – Buzz Aldrin, and Leland Givens. I’m going to conduct a symphony orchestra on Fly Me to the Moon and all that stuff. It’s insane. But we don’t have anything to do with it. Once you start to understand, just let go and let God, you have to have a good time in life. That’s why . . .
But don’t you think that it is very unusual that you’d be at the birth of so many of these things?
Yeah, but what can you do about it? You can’t stop it or start it. That’s my point.

No. So you just learn how to just let it happen and be strong enough, because you know, The Road Less Traveled – M. Scott Peck, right? – he says – he starts the book: life is a struggle. As soon as you accept that, it’s going to get easier. To learn – Basie said the same thing. He says, “Youngblood, it’s about hills and valleys. Anybody can handle the hills.” That’s a metaphor for success. The valleys are the ones that will test you as a human being.
